name: LapBar
author: Gregor Skrt
description: Your Strava in the Omarchy bar: the latest activity with route, stats, kudos and records by name, totals per sport for the day, week, month and year, a calendar of all your years, and fitness, fatigue and form worked out on your own computer, with optional motivational nudges. Needs a paid Strava subscription (Strava requires one to create an API app) and your own free API app; a guided setup walks you through it. Credentials stay in your keyring; nothing is sent anywhere but to Strava.

barWidget.description: Latest Strava activity, kudos and records, totals, calendar, fitness and form. Charts for every ride.

schema.label: Refresh interval (seconds)
schema.description: How often to ask Strava for new data (60 to 3600 seconds). Also settable from the widget menu. LapBar reads Strava's own usage counters and keeps itself inside the daily allowance: automatic refreshes pause at 60% of it, leaving room for manual refreshes (the refresh button, opening the panel), which work until 90%.

schema.label: Bar cycle interval (seconds)
schema.description: The bar button rotates through the latest activity, this week's total, kudos and PRs, and your training load compared with last week. 0 keeps it on the latest activity.

schema.label: Training load measure
schema.description: What 'ahead of / behind last week' compares: time (works for every sport), distance, or effort (Strava's Relative Effort, needs a heart-rate device; falls back to time).

schema.label: Store older activities in the background (per refresh)
schema.description: LapBar keeps the complete second-by-second data of every activity, GPS included, in ~/.local/share/lapbar (one Strava request each, downloaded once). The newest ride is stored automatically; this many older ones are added on each refresh, newest first, until everything is stored. The number is scaled down as the day's request allowance fills up and stops at 40% of it. 0 turns the background download off (a chart you open is still downloaded on demand).

schema.label: FTP (watts, cycling)
schema.description: Your functional threshold power, shown as a large number in the popup and used for power-based training load on rides with a power meter. Strava's API does not give it to LapBar with the permissions it asks for, so enter it here or from the widget menu (0 = unknown). The menu can also estimate it from your ride history.

schema.label: History for the calendar (years)
schema.description: How many earlier years to download from Strava so the calendar can page back to them. 0 = this year only; 99 = everything Strava has. Each year is downloaded once (one request per 200 activities) and stored on this computer, a couple of years per refresh so the request allowance is never at risk.
